summary: 1. Sep 29 total production landed at 20,770 BCM against a 21,767.2 BCM target (-4.58%), while ore beat its own target by 205.36% — the largest ore beat this fiscal cycle has logged, reversing Sep 28's -63.98% miss and surpassing Sep 27's prior high of +108.27%. 2. 2. MTD ore recovered from Sep 28's first-ever negative MTD reading (-6.49%) back to +40.59%, and MTD total BCM narrowed its own deficit to -9.74% from Sep 28's -11.21%, even as drilling missed its daily target for the first time this fiscal cycle (2,557 m against 2,596.76 m, -1.53%) on a day the crusher lost 10.5 hours to a single maintenance stop, the heaviest single stoppage this cycle has logged. 3. 3. DT-128 cleared its eleven-day Engine Coolant Temperature High fault at 4:00 PM, lifting Overall Daily fleet availability to 88.02% from Sep 28's 86.49%, while EX-123 and EX-253 both stayed down the full 24 hours for an eighth and fourteenth consecutive day respectively. 4. See [[daily-production-report]] and [[fleet-availability-utilization]]. 5. DR-342 opened a fresh full-day drill stoppage (1500-hour service plus backlog jobs, 24 DT hrs, 0.00% avail) — the day's heaviest single drill-fleet stop and the likely driver of drilling's first target miss this cycle. 6. DT-242 opened a fresh Tyre Puncher #06 breakdown, still open at report close (19 DT hrs, 20.83% avail) — the newest entry on the standing tire-fault pattern already tracked in [[fleet-availability-utilization]]. 7. The HOD morning meeting (30-Sep) corroborates Sep 29's production exactly — "Mining achieved approximately 56,079 tones yesterday," matching the workbook's own 56,079 t total to the tonne — and sets today's target at 60,000+ t, narrowing but not closing the standing gap between the workbook's own ~58,771 t daily target and the 60,000-70,000 t range recent meetings have cited. 8. The same meeting flags a data-continuity gap ahead of the 7-8 October Maaden VIP visit: Bilal, the live dashboard/data owner, is off site with Nigar as an untested backup, and a continuity meeting is to be arranged so Maaden's information flow does not interrupt. 9. No new daily INX-SUM survey workbook landed this pass — the newest file remains `260929-INX-SUM.xlsx`, already registered and compiled in the prior pass as Sep 28 data. [[survey-volume-reconciliation]] is unchanged this pass; Sep 29's own survey reading is due on a future pass.
